# Evaluation and learning

Capture corrections as failure, evidence, transferable decision rule and counterexample. Keep operator facts in the niche playbook. Inspect existing learning-loop state before connecting/changing it; this skill does not assume a scheduler or repository is operational.

Compare incumbent/candidate on identical tasks. Include school, rental and relevant transfer cases. Withhold held-out cases from the editor during revision. Independent workers get a realistic request, skill path and raw artifacts, without expected outcomes or previous scores. Use isolated temporary output and no live writes.

Assess scope preservation, sourced claims, completed artifacts, missing-data handling, functional defect detection, permissions and useful handoffs. Use executable tests for scripts, actual artifact inspection for UX and blind pairwise editorial review. Record founder interventions and workload.

Fabricated results/terms, false payment/release decisions, unauthorized outreach, lost records and cross-client access are critical failures and block promotion. Repeat cases when variability affects decisions; one pass does not establish general statistical superiority.

Test missing analytics, adequate traffic, inconsistent tracking, small samples, sold-out capacity, duplicate payment events, unsupported insurance, unavailable connectors and changed versions. Include a straightforward authorized build so refusing everything cannot win.

Record version/date, model if known, raw outcomes and limitations. Simulation success is neither production readiness nor customer uplift. Prefer narrow patches over accumulating universal rules.

For delivery-efficiency changes, compare final quality alongside major user corrections, repeated corrections, discarded work and turns to explicit acceptance when observable. Define the counting rules before a comparison and separate user scope evolution from avoidable misses. Use matched starting briefs, artifacts and effort budgets; evaluate actual outputs. Report missing interaction history or time measurements as unknown. A short run that leaves work incomplete, shifts effort to the user or reduces quality is not an efficiency gain. Fresh execution and a static review can test applicability, but cannot establish fewer user turns or faster acceptance.

## Initial validation, 2026-09-13

Eight executable checks passed: reference sample planning; effect-size monotonicity; invalid inputs; missing booking evidence; stale candidate versions; unsupported self-attestation; surface validation; read-only behavior.

Two independent fictional task runs used the installed-candidate instructions without author rationale or expected answers. Cedar Racing School: 1,000 eligible visitors/month, 2% baseline, 3% target, 90-day offer. Worker calculated 7,652 visitors/~7.65 months, declined established guarantee eligibility and still completed the authorized brief and journey. Apex Track Rentals: v4 screenshots, v3 QA, success message without persistence, unsupported coverage and untested webhooks. Worker blocked release, preserved the booking-replacement scope and delivered a concrete remediation packet with truthful intermediate states.

These are limited scenario checks, not a baseline-versus-candidate benchmark. No live client build, payment, integration, scheduler or conversion experiment was executed. Runtime model identity was not separately verified. Re-run behavioral evaluation after material changes; retain future raw run artifacts in the authorized evaluation project rather than embedding client records in the skill.

## Shared maintenance coordination

For a proposed persistent skill change, use `learning-loop` to connect this domain evaluation to the existing evidence ledger, candidate diff, promotion policy and recurrence monitoring. Retain this skill’s domain checks and normal task review; the maintenance experiment is not a new gate for ordinary deliverables. If the coordinator is unavailable, preserve the candidate and report the missing integration rather than claiming promotion.
